_comment: Phase 10.A/C -- illustrative OpenSearch Security role definitions, NOT applied automatically by any script in this repo (doing so requires a cluster-admin credential this codebase does not hold -- OPENSEARCH_USER/PASSWORD in .env is intentionally just one shared app credential today). Apply each role with the OpenSearch Security plugin's REST API, e.g.: curl -u <admin> -X PUT https://<host>:9200/_plugins/_security/api/roles/recipe_writer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- <<< '<that role's body below>' -- then map real users/credentials to these roles instead of sharing one over-privileged account across ingest, query, and audit-review.

recipe_writer._comment: Used by ingest.py across every stage. Can write recipe/document indexes but has NO access to recipes-audit-log -- ingestion should never be able to tamper with the audit trail it doesn't even write to.

recipe_reader._comment: Used by query.py's grounding/refine search calls. Read-only, and still explicitly excludes the audit index -- a query-serving credential has no legitimate reason to read the compliance log.

audit_writer._comment: Used by log_audit_event() (query.py, every stage-5+ query). Can index new audit records but explicitly CANNOT delete or update existing ones -- an audit trail that the query path itself can edit or purge after the fact isn't trustworthy for compliance.

audit_admin._comment: For compliance reviewers / monitor.py / policy_registry.py and retention (ISM) management only. Separate credential from audit_writer -- the role that reads and administers the audit trail should not be the same role the live query path writes through.
